evidence.quote: | NetEndOfMonth days -> DateOnly(issueDate.Year, issueDate.Month, DateTime.DaysInMonth(issueDate.Year, issueDate.Month)).AddDays days
| true, days when days > 0 && days <= 365 -> Ok(Some(NetEndOfMonth days))

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The end-of-month due-date rule is added to `Invoicing.dueDate` in Summa.Ledger (Tier 1). The form parsing and validation of the terms text is in Summa.Web.Engine (Tier 2). The storage codec change only maps the new case to and from JSON. Nothing is decided in Tier 3 or Tier 4.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: No new effect is introduced. `dueDate`, the parser, `termsText` and the codec are all pure, and no clock, I/O or console access is added.

evidence.quote: | _ -> Error "Terms are a number of days between 0 and 365, optionally followed by EOM, ..."

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The `Net {days} EOM` wording is written as two separate literals, one in `Documents.termsText` and one in `Invoicing.termsWords`. This follows how the existing `Net` case is already handled. The 1..365 bound and the full error message are also repeated in both the EOM and plain-days branches. The copies agree, so this is restatement rather than contradiction.

evidence.quote: | true, day when day >= 1 && day <= 28 -> Ok(Some(DayOfNextMonth day))

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The due-date rule and the ordinal wording (`ordinal`, `termsDue`) are added in Summa.Ledger (Tier 1). The form parsing is in the Tier 2 engine. Tier 3 and Tier 4 only call these.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: No effect is added. All new code (`ordinal`, `termsDue`, the `dueDate` case, the codec case and the parser branch) is pure.

evidence.quote: if day >= 1 && day <= 28 then Ok(DayOfNextMonth day) else Error "day must be from 1 to 28"
| true, day when day >= 1 && day <= 28 -> Ok(Some(DayOfNextMonth day))

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The ordinal wording is defined once, in `termsDue`, and used by both `Documents.termsText` and `Invoicing.termsWords`. This is better than change set 1 for the new terms. However, the 1..28 day limit is a bare literal in two places, the storage decoder and the engine parser, with no shared definition. The copies agree today but could drift. The `Net {days} EOM` wording is still written twice, and the long error message is repeated three times.
